races.name: Education Network Handicap

runners_data.name: Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Consistent 7f performer at Standard going with three places and a win from five similar-surface runs; Connor Beasley is a strong booking and the horse's prominent style is perfectly suited to pressing Room Service from the off with tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Rajeko
runners_data.note: 127-day absence is a significant concern for a hold-up horse that must produce a late run; best form came over 7f on Standard, and if fitness holds he could be a big-price closer if the pace quickens late.

runners_data.name: Bobby Bennu
runners_data.note: Roger Varian-trained prominent racer who won over 7f on Good going; 28 days since last run is manageable, and his natural handy position gives him every chance if he can reproduce near his OR=92 best.

runners_data.name: Korker
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in finishes, which is a serious concern in a 7f handicap where even a moderate pace will test his resolution in the final furlong; form figures of 0-0806 over 6f-7f on good ground tell a cautionary story.

runners_data.name: Tremolo
runners_data.note: Strong form record including wins on Standard going, but 310 days off the track is a glaring unknown; by nature a prominent racer, he is squeezed into midfield by the field's pace density, meaning he races against type here.

runners_data.name: Metal Merchant
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by inclination but shifted to the midfield band on the map; form of /00-00 offers no encouragement, and Ian Toomey's small string (1/2 in 14 days) provides no meaningful trainer angle.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Wilko
runners_data.note: Best effort recently was a 2nd over 7f on Good, suggesting the class is there, but Kevin Ryan's 14-day strike rate is a modest 1/39 and the horse has finished no closer than 4th in his last four; hold-up style suits a faster-run race.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: Won a 7f handicap on Good going and placed over the same trip, giving him genuine course-and-distance credentials; however, he is a natural prominent type crammed into midfield here, meaning he must race out of role.

runners_data.name: Sir Albert
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo carries a light 121lbs and has a placed effort on Standard going; prominent style fits the likely race shape well, and PJ McDonald is an astute booking for a horse that could be competitive if getting cover early.

runners_data.name: Caviar Cowboy
runners_data.note: Five consecutive runs on Standard going with a win and four places, giving him excellent surface form; naturally a prominent racer by style, he is mapped to midfield due to congestion, reducing the chance he gets his preferred position.

runners_data.name: Room Service
runners_data.note: Top weight at 142lbs after a 266-day absence is the dominant concern for the confirmed leader; class is clear at OR=105, but absence combined with burden on a Standard to Slow surface means stamina in the closing stages is the key question.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 7yo has two wins from 15 similar-going runs but recent form figures of 489000 suggest he is struggling for his best; hold-up style demands a strong pace that this race may not deliver.

runners_data.name: Supido
runners_data.note: William Buick's booking for Ian Williams immediately elevates interest; won over 8f on Good and placed on Standard going, and as a genuine hold-up type he is best served by a race with pace — worth monitoring in-running to see if he gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Nikovo
runners_data.note: Older handicapper whose sim-going record of 10th-best from 15 similar-surface runs is underwhelming; Michael Herrington's yard is in form (3/17 in 14 days) but the horse's prominent style means he will be racing into a competitive front group.

races.paceDynamic: Room Service leads from the front at OR=105 carrying 142lbs, and with no genuine challenger to that position, sets a controlled, unhurried gallop on a Standard to Slow surface that will keep early sectionals measured. Yorkshire and Sir Albert are the most likely to press from prominent positions, while Bobby Bennu and Nikovo will also race handy, creating a mildly competitive early order without any horse likely to force a genuinely pressured pace. The relatively sedate tempo over 7f on a flat AW track shapes this as a race where the leading group retains a meaningful advantage into the straight, favouring prominently-raced horses who can sustain their effort rather than those making late ground. The field carries a significant overload of prominent types — Tremolo, Caviar Cowboy, and Brighton Boy are genuine prominent racers by nature, but cannot all secure their preferred positions; Yorkshire, Sir Albert, and Bobby Bennu are most likely to actually settle close to Room Service, with the others shuffled back against their will.

scenarios.body: If Room Service dictates a steady pace and the prominently-placed horses track comfortably, setting up a sustained duel from 2f out.

scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains truly minimal and Room Service's class allows it to control margins despite the big weight.
scenarios.body: If the pace remains truly minimal and Room Service's class allows it to control margins despite the big weight.

scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race as multiple prominent types push forward from behind Room Service, stringing out the field and burning off the leaders.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens mid-race as multiple prominent types push forward from behind Room Service, stringing out the field and burning off the leaders.

scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos, Tactical Scramble

scenarios.body: If the redistribution effect causes a contested early order with Tremolo, Brighton Boy, or Caviar Cowboy pushing unexpectedly into the front rank and forcing a faster tempo.

watchPoints.text: Room Service (142lbs, 266 days off) — if the pace slackens before the 2f pole, watch whether the weight begins to tell and a prominent challenger such as Yorkshire or Sir Albert accelerates past.

Tremolo (310-day absence, natural prominent type mapped to midfield) — monitor in the first furlong whether he attempts to push forward into his natural position; if he does, it could create an unplanned pace injection.

Supido with William Buick aboard — as the hold-up scenario's most likely beneficiary, watch his position tracking into the straight; if he is still travelling well 2f out in a genuine pace meltdown, he becomes the main danger.

Brighton Boy and Caviar Cowboy — both natural prominent types currently sitting in midfield on the map; if either secures an early prominent pitch in the actual race, the pace picture becomes busier and Room Service's lead more contested.

Standard to Slow going confirmation — the going report consistently lists this race as Standard to Slow, which will stretch stamina late; any horse showing signs of dwelling or pulling hard in the early stages should be downgraded.

races.name: JenningsBet Chipchase Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Honour
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's four-year-old is a natural stalker who has strong Goodwood form on good ground; the switch to Newcastle AW Standard to Slow is worth noting but Buick's positioning just off Marvelman should suit his hold-on-the-pace profile, and his one win in the last five came over this trip.

runners_data.name: Wiltshire
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Standard AW (Haydock) last time and Fallon rides him well; a true hold-up horse who needs the pace to collapse to make his finishing run count, and headgear (tongue tie) helps him settle — sim-going strike rate of 8/15 suggests he handles it but needs a fast tempo.

runners_data.name: Zoum Zoum
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's five-year-old is genuinely a front-running or prominent type who will be shuffled back into the pack by the volume of pace rivals; only one sim-going run from 15 attempts limits confidence, and racing out of his preferred position blunts his chances markedly here.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Heather
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's sprinter carries a strong sim-going record (11/15) and finished second twice over 5f on this surface; naturally front-running in style but the field's pace concentration means she will be crowded out of her preferred berth, which is a significant handicap to overcome.

runners_data.name: Marvelman
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old is the only confirmed lead horse and the clear pace anchor of the race; his best form is over 7f on soft ground and he has not run for 133 days, so his ability to maintain a strong gallop over 6f on Standard to Slow AW after a long absence is the central unknown in this race.

runners_data.name: Bloodsweatandtyres
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and a natural front-runner from Brian Ellison's yard; he has only three runs on record, one win over 7f on Standard AW, and with an OR of 76 he is significantly outclassed here at Group 3 level — being pushed into the midfield cluster does him no favours tactically either.

runners_data.name: Diligent Harry
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's eight-year-old has won twice on Standard AW and over 5-6f, making him well-suited to this surface; Saffie Osborne navigates him efficiently from a prominent position (headgear: probably aids focus), and his two recent wins on this type of ground underline his claims.

runners_data.name: Ferrous
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's hold-up runner has a solid sim-going record (9/15) and has placed over 6f on Standard AW; Connor Beasley will need a truly run race to produce his late surge, and 85 days off means fitness is a mild query, but his style is genuine and consistent.

runners_data.name: Heathcliff
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's five-year-old ran just seven days ago and has strong AW form (2W/8P on sim going); a natural front-runner by style who will find himself competing for midfield space in this congested pace scenario, though his recent fitness and sim-going familiarity are genuine assets if he can slot in.

runners_data.name: Noble Champion
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse with a Group-level win on good ground at 7f; Newcastle AW and Standard to Slow is outside his strongest going profile (1/8 sim-going), and Mulrennan will need Marvelman to set a true gallop to give him a race to run into — his class makes him dangerous if conditions align.

runners_data.name: Paborus
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's five-year-old has not run for 364 days, which is a serious fitness flag whatever the talent; he has winning form on Standard AW at 7f and his OR of 109 is competitive, but returning from a year off in a Group 3 sprint over 6f is a significant ask — Callum Rodriguez will need him to be spot-on first time back.

runners_data.name: Poet Master
runners_data.note: K R Burke's consistent six-year-old has placed five times in recent starts but not won since dropping back; his best form is at 7f on good or soft ground and 6f on AW is the minimum trip for him — Sam James will try to slot him mid-to-rear of the prominent group, but he needs things to happen late.

races.paceDynamic: Marvelman is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner field and, critically, is the only horse likely to press the early fractions from the front — with Standard to Slow conditions at Newcastle AW, he should set a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than a breakneck pace. This creates a race that will be run at an honest but not brutal tempo, with Marvelman able to dictate terms largely unchallenged, conserving enough for the finish. The field contains a heavy concentration of prominent-style horses — Zoum Zoum, Heavenly Heather, Heathcliff, and Bloodsweatandtyres are all natural front-runners or stalkers pushed into a midfield mapping because there simply is not enough room for them to race where they want; of these, Diligent Harry and Symbol Of Honour are best placed to secure the prominent positions just off Marvelman's heels given their class and recent form. With one clean pace-setter and a compressed midfield group, this race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or just off the pace — true hold-up horses face an uphill task if the tempo is controlled and there is no late collapse to exploit.

scenarios.body: If Marvelman gets a clean lead and sets a fair but sustainable gallop, allowing the best-positioned prominent runners to stalk and strike.

scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Battle It Out

scenarios.body: If the redistributed prominent types (Heathcliff, Zoum Zoum, Heavenly Heather) find their natural positions early and force a genuinely competitive pace chase.

scenarios.body: If the start is messy or Marvelman misses the break, removing the single pace anchor and creating a falsely-run sprint.

watchPoints.text: Marvelman's stamina for 6f on Standard to Slow AW after 133 days off is the race's central question — if he fades inside the final furlong he could trigger a dramatic reshuffle that overturns the likely leader-biased verdict.

The cluster of displaced prominent types — Zoum Zoum, Heavenly Heather, Heathcliff, and Bloodsweatandtyres — will jostle hard for position in the early stages, raising the risk of interference or crowding that could compromise runners tracking the pace.

Paborus returns from a full year off (364 days) in a Group 3 sprint — if Bethell has him spot-on he could outrun his likely drifting SP, but a race-fitness concern of this magnitude in fast company is a material risk flag.

Noble Champion's sim-going record (1/8) is modest for Standard to Slow AW, and if the surface rides slower than expected tonight his hold-up profile could be further compromised by a lack of pace to close into in the final furlong.

Diligent Harry won twice at 5-6f on Standard AW earlier this season — watch whether Saffie Osborne targets a position immediately behind Marvelman, as securing that rail-tracking slot could be the decisive positional move in this race.

races.name: JenningsBet Festival Northumberland Vase Handicap (Consolation Race For Northumberland Plate) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Charging Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who appreciates similar ground (6/15 sim-going record shows 1W2P), drops back to 16f after two runs here at that trip; 55 days off adds a fitness query, but James Owen's yard has won 9 from 50 in the 14-day window suggesting horses are fit; penalty for sitting last in a 20-runner field is severe if pace is modest.

runners_data.name: Chemistry
runners_data.note: The only genuine pace-setter in the race and therefore holds a unique tactical asset; has won over 17f at Goodwood at good which is the most relevant form, but STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reflects that dictating at the front is arguably racing slightly out of her comfort zone from a prominent rather than lead base; Standard to Slow going should not inconvenience her.

runners_data.name: Alphonse Le Grande
runners_data.note: Irish raider who wants to race prominently but recent form is poor (587-00); has placed twice over similar trips at comparable going, but the T14:0/4 trainer strike rate is weak and a 50-day break raises readiness doubts; seven-year-old who needs this trip to be run at a true stamina-testing pace.

runners_data.name: Shrimp Shady
runners_data.note: Has a strong recent form profile (44121) with wins at 18f Goodwood and 16f Newcastle on good-to-soft-equivalent ground, making this trip and going combination squarely in his wheelhouse; prominent-racing four-year-old who will be ideally placed just behind Chemistry; Andrew Balding's yard is in solid 14-day form (12/57).

runners_data.name: Artisan Dancer
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with two wins at 16f on standard going and a Goodwood run at 12f last time (10th); the drop back to longer trip suits and 27 days since last run is fine; Cieren Fallon takes the ride for Charlie Johnston whose yard shows 4/34 in the 14-day window — workmanlike but not hot.

runners_data.name: Sax Appeal
runners_data.note: Consistent stayer who rarely wins but posts frame finishes (383653) and has placed 7 from 15 times on sim-going; fitted with a hood which may help him focus in a big field; six days since last run is an asset for freshness and Charlie Johnston has a second string here; 16f+ has been his domain at Goodwood this season.

runners_data.name: Laafy
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran whose recent form string (7/08-0) reads poorly — 13th at Goodwood, 8th at Haydock, aborted run in between; the visor is retained but nothing in recent evidence suggests he can recapture his better days; prominent style means he will be fighting for a position he may not get in this field.

runners_data.name: Premiere Ligne
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose two best efforts came over 20f and 18f at Good, suggesting he needs a strong stamina test to produce his best; sim-going record shows only 1 from 15 which is a concern; 15 days since last run and Hughie Morrison T14:2/10 strike rate is low — needs the race to truly stay to have a chance.

runners_data.name: Believitanducan
runners_data.note: Three wins from five starts over 16f-21f including two at 16f Goodwood and one at 20f Heatherslaw on soft — this horse handles big fields and stamina trips; prominent-racing five-year-old trained by Alan King (T14:3/11), with William Buick taking a notable booking; sim-going record shows 0W1P which is the one soft spot, but trip and style fit are excellent.

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature with a solid record at 14f-17f on good going (1W2P from 14 sim-going runs), but a 309-day absence (252 days jumps-included) is a massive flag; pushed back into midfield by the field's prominent saturation, so races entirely against his natural style — both the layoff and the positional compromise discount his chance significantly.

runners_data.name: Hermetic
runners_data.note: Young four-year-old who has placed at 16f on soft (6th) and 12f good (4th); limited profile makes assessment difficult but the 131 OR suggests connections believe the trip is within range; Luke Morris rides for Ian Williams (T14:1/47, modest) and 20 days since last run is fine — but this is a big step into the unknown over 2m½f.

runners_data.name: Savrola
runners_data.note: A genuine front-running type by record (1W at 16f STA, placed at 16f SOF and 13f SOF) who is being displaced into midfield by the queue of prominent horses ahead of him; 14 days since last run suits, Dianne Sayer T14:0/5 is low; he'll need to fight aggressively out of the gate to reclaim anything like his natural position, which will cost energy.

runners_data.name: Arc Zoosve
runners_data.note: Has won five of his last six starts including three over 16f on standard going, giving him the strongest recent form in the bottom half of the weights; naturally a prominent type but bumped back into midfield by field density — if Dougie Costello can push forward from the gate the form entitles him to be competitive, though racing against his preferred style is a real cost at this trip.

runners_data.name: St Faz
runners_data.note: Irish raider with three wins over 14f-16f including on standard going, making the trip and surface fine; has placed twice in similar-going conditions from four attempts; mapped to midfield despite his prominent nature — Mikey Sheehy will need to ride aggressively early in a 20-runner field, and a 27-day break is unproblematic.

runners_data.name: Fast Fred
runners_data.note: Six-year-old whose entire recent form is over 11f-12f (best wins at 12f GOO and 12f STA), making this step up to 2m½f a very significant question mark regardless of style; his headgear (hood/p) may help concentration but trip stamina is the primary doubt; pushed back from a prominent role into midfield compresses his chance further.

runners_data.name: Boxing Great
runners_data.note: Won over 16f STA last time (OR was lower) but followed up with 8th at 18f GOO and 6th at 14f GOO, showing inconsistency; fitted with a hood and races for Karl Thornton (T14:0/8); 15 days since last run is fine; natural prominent type forced into midfield, and the 18f last time showed he may not quite get this 2m½f trip convincingly.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with wins at 16f GOO and 16f GOO plus a second at 16f SOF showing excellent staying form for a young horse; 5 days since last run is notably quick for a stayer and warrants monitoring; Tim Easterby has 14 wins from 112 runners — volume yard running to form; true prominent type shuffled back, so David Allan must decide early whether to push forward or accept midfield.

runners_data.name: Haveyoumissedme
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose recent form is over 10f-12f (3rd, 7th, 2nd, 5th, 3rd) with a strong Standard going profile (8/15 with 4 places); this step to 2m½f is a stamina stretch for a horse running consistently at shorter; Iain Jardine T14:3/41 is modest; his natural prominent style is hampered by being mapped back — and the trip extension is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who specialises on Standard going (8/15, 2W6P including wins at 16f and 12f STA); 59-day break is the question mark but the form suggests he comes alive fresh; Rhys Elliott (5lb claimer) takes significant pressure off the weight

races.paceDynamic: Chemistry is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field over 2m½f at Newcastle on a Standard to Slow surface, and with no genuine rival willing to press her early, she is set to control pace from the outset at a tempo she can dictate entirely on her own terms. Behind her, the prominent positions will be fiercely contested: Shrimp Shady, Artisan Dancer, Sax Appeal, Alphonse Le Grande, Believitanducan and Hermetic all want to race handy, meaning the early jostling for the first few berths will be intense. Hold-up horses Charging Thunder, Clansman, Premiere Ligne and Day Trader will settle towards the rear, likely a significant distance off the pace given the crowded midfield ahead of them, which could leave them with an enormous amount of ground to make up in the straight. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Brosna Town, Savrola, Arc Zoosve, St Faz, Fast Fred, Boxing Great, Treasure Islands and Haveyoumissedme are all genuine prominent racers who will be shuffled back into a congested midfield against their will, blunting their effectiveness; of these, Savrola and Arc Zoosve have the strongest profiles to actually fight their way into a forward position if they commit aggressively from the gate. The tactical verdict is clear: with a single unhurried pace-setter in Chemistry controlling a steady gallop over a stamina trip, and closers likely anchored deep in a large, slow-moving pack, horses that can slot comfortably just behind the leader in second or third — especially those with confirmed form at this trip and on similar ground — are best placed to pounce entering the straight without burning energy fighting for position.

races.name: JenningsBet Northumberland Plate Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Prydwen
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid Standard-going form (1W1P in 15 sim-going runs); trainer George Scott has a modest 14-day strike rate (1/16) and 48 days off raises a fitness question, but the 2m½f trip and controlled pace of this race suit his profile well.|

runners_data.name: Tashkhan
runners_data.note: 231 days off (112 days since jockey booking) is a significant concern for an 8-year-old, and Brian Ellison's 14-day record is modest (1/25); best form came on Soft-Heavy going and his single similar-going run over 20f produced no placed effort, so this trip on AW Standard to Slow is a sizable stamina/surface question.|

runners_data.name: Circus Of Rome
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter in the field, likely to control from flag to finish at a steady tempo on a Standard to Slow surface; OR=98 with two wins and four places in five similar-going runs, this 4-year-old is racing beyond his usual 8-14f range and stamina is an open question over 2m½f, but his front-running role gives him every tactical advantage in a slowly-run affair. Note the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) indicates some positional stretch.|

runners_data.name: Align The Stars
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Standard for Charlie Johnston and holds strong form credentials (1W1P in 15 similar-going runs); the headgear note (p) and Daniel Muscutt in the saddle suggest he is held in good regard, and his hold-up style positions him ideally if the race develops with a controlled pace.|

runners_data.name: Spirit Mixer
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's runner has a 1W2P record in 15 similar-going runs and won over 16f on Soft; prominent style should allow him to track Circus Of Rome, but eight career runs over this sort of trip suggest he handles the distance and the stable's 14-day record (14/68) is competitive.|

runners_data.name: Bahadur
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on this lightly-raced 4-year-old, adding significant jockey confidence; three wins in four similar-going runs and a win over 16f on Standard make him interesting, though his trainer (S Woods) has a blank 14-day record (0/9) and his last run (10th over 20f at Goodwood) raises a distance doubt.|

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Won over 14f on Soft for Ian Williams and has placed form over 16f, making the trip plausible; a prominent racer, though recent form (8240-9) is uninspiring and the 21-day return is straightforward.|

runners_data.name: Team Player
runners_data.note: Four wins in 13 similar-going runs is a strong stat for this 4-year-old, including victories over 14f and 16f; the headgear (tp) and Ewan Whillans' modest trainer record (1/12 over 14 days) are minor negatives, but the prominent style and strong Standard/Soft record make him a live contender.|

runners_data.name: Blazeon Five
runners_data.note: Three wins from five similar-going runs including wins over 16f on Standard and Soft — strong course/going profile; 71 days off is the main concern, though Alan King's string runs to a 4/10 14-day record, and the prominent running style could be ideal for this controlled-pace race.|

runners_data.name: Elysian Flame
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old with headgear (p) and a 5-runner claim from apprentice Rhys Elliott (5lb claim); won over 16f on Soft and has proven stamina, but recent form (4th, 5th, 1st, 4th, 5th) is inconsistent and the trainer's 14-day record is blank (0/2).|

runners_data.name: Asgard's Captain
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Goodwood and has solid Soft-going form, but his natural prominent style means he is one of the horses genuinely competing for a forward position in a crowded field — the redistribution flag reflects real pressure on his preferred spot; Saffie Osborne takes the ride and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) signals meaningful positional risk.|

runners_data.name: Saint Etienne
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's second string is a hold-up type with headgear (t); form figures of 7-9047 are modest and his best performances in similar going come over shorter trips (9-11f), making the 2m½f a potential stamina stretch over and above his poor recent form.|

runners_data.name: Synergism
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's charge has three wins from seven similar-going runs over 14-16f on Standard — outstanding course/going form; Luke Morris in the saddle and the prominent style should allow him to sit just off Circus Of Rome and deliver a sustained challenge, making him one of the most profiles-aligned runners in the field.|

runners_data.name: Tribal Star
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness's 5-year-old is a genuine prominent type who races with headgear (p) and has proven form over 16-18f on Standard; he is one of seven prominent types competing for limited forward positions and his STYLE_FIT (0.92) reflects that he may be forced to race further back than preferred — Adam Caffrey rides.|

runners_data.name: Ride The Thunder
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 4-year-old won over 10f and placed over 14f, but has yet to prove he truly stays 2m½f; a genuine prominent runner who faces the same positional challenge as other front-rank types in this field, and the step up in trip from his usual 10-14f range is significant — STYLE_FIT (0.90) reflects both the positional and distance concern.|

runners_data.name: Moon Over Miami
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's runner has no wins or places in nine similar-going runs, which is a damning stat for a horse heading to 2m½f on Standard to Slow; placed over 16f on Good, but the Standard-going record (3/9, 0W0P) and the redistribution from his natural prominent position both weigh against him.|

runners_data.name: Aqwaam
runners_data.note: Three wins from eight similar-going runs but his most recent Standard-going outing produced an 11th-place finish over 12f; Ian Williams has a second string here and Mikey Sheehy takes the mount — a natural prominent type forced further back than ideal, and his best trip on Standard looks shorter than today's 2m½f.|

runners_data.name: Zanndabad
runners_data.note: Won over 22f on Soft and 20f on Good — strong stamina credentials that make this trip no concern; however, A J Martin's 14-day record is blank (0/5), the 50-day absence is notable, and his 8/18 finish at Goodwood last time was disappointing. A genuine prominent type who will struggle to find his natural position.|

runners_data.name: Gentleman Joe
runners_data.note: Matt Crawley's 8-year-old is a hold-up type with headgear (tp) and an 8-year-old profile that suggests consistency is not a strength; form of 426-90 is poor and the trainer's 14-day record is blank (0/2), though 16f form on Soft and Good provides some evidence of stamina.|

runners_data.name: Kirchner
runners_data.note: James Owen's 4-year-old has only one similar-going run in five (5th over 12f STA) and his best form has come at shorter distances (8-12f); a genuine prominent type pushed back by the overcrowded field, and the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) reflects both positional and trip concerns — Cieren Fallon takes the ride.|

races.paceDynamic: Circus Of Rome is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 20 over 2m½f on a Standard to Slow Newcastle AW surface, and with no genuine rival prepared to press from the front, he should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the outset. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a lone leader over this trip setting his own rhythm creates a scenario where the race is truly run to suit those who can travel economically just off the pace and produce a sustained finish, rather than those who require a truly strong pace to close from deep. The field contains a significant surplus of prominent-style horses — Asgard's Captain, Zanndabad, Tribal Star, Ride The Thunder, Moon Over Miami, Aqwaam, and Kirchner are all genuine prominent types who cannot all hold their natural position, meaning several will be forced to race further back than ideal. Given the likely controlled tempo set by Circus Of Rome, the race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven ability to travel smoothly in a slowly-run contest and pick off a tiring leader, as well as any prominent racer able to genuinely slot just behind Circus Of Rome and sustain their effort over the final quarter-mile.

Synergism's profile — three wins from seven similar-going runs, 14-16f Standard form, Prescott/Morris combination — makes him the most dangerous single runner to Circus Of Rome if he can sit directly behind the leader and exploit the slow pace, watch for him to be ridden aggressively into a prominent tracking position from the start.

runners_data.name: The Caltonian
runners_data.note: Has a course win on this surface and simulated-going figures show solid form (2W3P in 15 runs), but a 75-day break and hold-up style mean he needs others to set a fast enough pace to close into; the blinkers are a notable headgear flag and Paul Mulrennan knows this horse well.

runners_data.name: Topwarrior
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old naturally wants to race prominently but faces competition for that berth from multiple rivals; his sim-going record on standard surfaces is modest (1W2P from 10) and his recent form shows a loss of form on softer ground — he is one whose chance is tempered by not getting his preferred racing position.

runners_data.name: Rapper's Delight
runners_data.note: Returned from 113 days off for Richard Spencer and Saffie Osborne, and the visor is a headgear switch worth noting; genuinely likes to race in the first two or three, but this field is too deep in forward-going types for him to guarantee that slot, and his best form is on slower going rather than AW standard.

runners_data.name: Al Najashi
runners_data.note: Five wins from nine on Standard going for Ollie Sangster is a striking statistic, and Callum Rodriguez is a sharp jockey for pace scenarios; nevertheless, this is a horse whose natural front-running style cannot be accommodated by all 14 runners, and he arrives on a 45-day break stepping back from 7f — the drop in trip may sharpen him but the positional squeeze is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Strike Red
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran for the Fahey yard who wants to be up with the pace, but his simulated-going record (0W1P from 15) is unimpressive and he has slipped to OR 87 — Warren Fentiman (3) claims 3lb, which helps the weight, but Strike Red is unlikely to secure the prominent berth his style demands.

runners_data.name: Cool Hoof Luke
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's OR 104 topweight is the confirmed front-runner and carries the highest weight in the field at 142lbs; his Standard-going record (2W3P from 8) is solid and he has won on this track, but the style-fit note reminds us that leading at a solo controlled tempo may not be his optimum mode — the weight burden is real.

runners_data.name: Fahrenheit Seven
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's five-year-old has a good record on Standard surfaces (3W4P from 15) and two consecutive wins on AW 5f standard last year suggest he handles this surface well; races prominently and is one of those genuinely in the mix for a forward position — Ray Dawson keeps the ride and a return to 6f from 5f is a slight unknown.

runners_data.name: Caburn
runners_data.note: James Tate's four-year-old has a flat simulated-going record (0W0P from 11) which is a concern despite strong form in general; Connor Beasley reunites and the hood (hg:p) is retained, but his best win came on soft — this standard-to-slow surface may not fully play to his strengths and he is 63 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Pocklington
runners_data.note: Geoff Oldroyd's five-year-old has a strong Standard-going record (3W6P from 14) and PJ McDonald is among the best jockeys at Newcastle; recent form figures of 2-1278 include wins on this surface and at this trip — a straightforward prominent racer who should genuinely hold his position in this field and is well-placed for the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Annaf
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's seven-year-old has a poor recent run of form (-77600) and his sim-going record shows little on Standard (0W1P from 15); hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace is swift enough to come off, but the weight and recent form make this a tough ask even if the shape falls right for Daniel Muscutt.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's veteran has gone 28 days since last run and has strong Standard-going form (1W5P from 15), including two second-place finishes at this trip on AW; the hood (hg:p) is retained and David Allan is experienced here — he is a genuine contender for the prominent position and holds each-way claims if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Tuco Salamanca
runners_data.note: William Buick takes over for Ollie Sangster and that is the single biggest jockey upgrade in the race; Standard-going form is exceptional (5W5P from 15) and his two wins on this course and surface confirm he handles the conditions — naturally prominent, one of those likely to get his position, and a horse whose form figures 159-16 show he knows how to win.

runners_data.name: Power Fizz
runners_data.note: William Haggas' four-year-old has won on Standard ground (2W2P from 8) and his most recent run was a winning one on AW 6f standard; however, 92 days off the track and being a natural pace-seeking type who cannot be accommodated at the front in this field means Cieren Fallon will need to find a different route — his class is genuine, his position is compromised.

runners_data.name: Knebworth
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes sends this six-year-old with two consecutive wins (1/6f/STA, 1/6f/STA) on this exact course and distance combination — that is the sharpest course form in the race; naturally prominent but pushed into a midfield slot by race congestion, Finley Marsh will need to find a clear run, but the surface form is undeniable and 91 days off may be an issue.

races.paceDynamic: Cool Hoof Luke is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to push him hard from the outset, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 6f Newcastle AW straight. The Standard To Slow going will compress sectionals and reward those who travel comfortably within themselves rather than those burning energy fighting for position — a lone pace-setter in a slowly-run race on AW typically leaves closers flat-footed, meaning those who can track the leader efficiently from second or third are ideally placed. Fahrenheit Seven, Caburn, Pocklington, Tuco Salamanca and Fivethousandtoone all have genuine claims to sit just off Cool Hoof Luke, though the redistribution note is critical: Power Fizz, Al Najashi, Knebworth, Rapper's Delight, Topwarrior and Strike Red are all naturally prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred berth in a 14-runner field, meaning several will be shuffled wider or further back than ideal. This race shape — controlled early pace, bunched midfield, late sprint — favours horses who can track the single leader at a manageable tempo and finish off powerfully, giving the edge to genuine prominent-to-midfield finishers over those redistibuted into false positions.

watchPoints.text: Tuco Salamanca — William Buick's booking onto the Ollie Sangster horse with the best Standard-going strike rate in the field (5W5P from 15) is the single most significant jockey upgrade; watch for him tracking Cool Hoof Luke closely and kicking between the final two poles.

Knebworth — two back-to-back wins on this exact course and trip on Standard going make him the most course-specific form horse in the race; if Finley Marsh can find a clear passage from a midfield position, the surface form gives him every right to be involved at the finish.

Cool Hoof Luke — confirmed lead, but the 142lb topweight on Standard To Slow ground is a significant burden; watch whether Rob Hornby allows him to stride on or is forced into a crawl that gifts the race to closers — the weight may blunt his finishing kick inside the final furlong.

Power Fizz — 92-day absence for William Haggas, returning on a surface he has won on, with Cieren Fallon booked; if he returns fresh and sharp he is unexposed at this trip and his last run was a win — the layoff is a watch point but the form before it is strong.

Positional scrimmage in the first furlong — with Al Najashi, Power Fizz, Knebworth, Topwarrior, Rapper's Delight and Strike Red all naturally wanting prominent positions that cannot all be filled, watch for crowding and jostling off the stalls that could unsettle any of the 14 runners drawn in unfavourable stalls.

runners_data.name: It's Only Fun

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine in good current form (4 from 20 in 14 days) and the horse has form at 16f on soft; however, his hold-up style is compromised here — the map pushes him into midfield traffic, and his two sim-going runs produced no wins or places.|

runners_data.name: Character Testing
runners_data.note: Not run for 68 days (previously was a 14-day reroute runner), wearing a tongue-plate, and his best form comes at 16-17f — this 1m4½f trip may be slightly short; his natural closer's role is squeezed by the field dynamics, though his two Goodwood placings at distance show genuine ability.|

runners_data.name: Billy Bathgate
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran with a remarkable consistency record — 15 from 15 on similar going including one win and seven places — and he handles this trip and surface with absolute confidence; 88 days off is the only query but trainer Whillans fires him fit.|

runners_data.name: Big Win

runners_data.name: Jujubella
runners_data.note: Ran only two days ago — freshness concern is significant and hard to discount at this level; naturally a hold-up performer, her recent form reads 6-0953 and she steps back to a more suitable 1m4½f, but the quick reappearance and sim-going figure (6 from 15 runs, one win) temper enthusiasm.|

runners_data.name: Golspie
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with 12 from 15 on similar surfaces, one win and three places; likely to track Romantic Spirit throughout from an early position and represents the main pacemaker's primary companion — his consistency on Standard ground makes him competitive if the leader tires.|

runners_data.name: Skinny Malinka
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who has only one run on comparable going from eight attempts — a significant concern — and her most recent start (0 after a break) came after a lengthy absence; steps back from 16f to 1m4½f but the going statistics are too thin to be confident.|

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Carries a fade warning tag for good reason — his form string (4/9-09) and histogram on Good ground shows repeated stopping in the final stages; on Standard to Slow ground where races tend to be truly run out, a horse who fades in the finish is particularly vulnerable here and must be treated with caution.|

runners_data.name: Sure And Stedfast
runners_data.note: The stable's higher-profile runner alongside Billy Bathgate, and PJ McDonald takes the ride; two placings in last five, including a second on soft and a third on Good, show he handles variation — however, a naturally hold-up horse who needs a stronger pace than Romantic Spirit is likely to provide.|

runners_data.name: Natzor
runners_data.note: Fade warning flag plus a recent form of 000-49 makes grim reading; 57 days off, tongue-plate on, and previous similar-going record shows one win from 15 but more losing positions at the sharp end — looks one for the shortlist of horses to oppose rather than back.|

runners_data.name: Arth's Gold
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon has nine winners from 52 in the 14-day window (strong current form) and the horse's sim-going record is outstanding — 13 from 15 with a win and five places; his recent course form at 12f on Standard gives him a significant edge, and he is a natural hold-up type whose best chance lies in tracking off the pace and finishing strongly.|

runners_data.name: Romantic Spirit
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter and the only genuine front-runner in this field; David Menuisier has three from 16 in the 14-day period and the horse's five consecutive runs on Standard at Newcastle all fit — 12 from 15 on similar going and an impressive course win — but the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that this trip (1m4½f) is slightly beyond his comfort zone based on recent placings at 11f.|

races.paceDynamic: Romantic Spirit is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 14-strong field and, critically, faces no genuine pace pressure — Golspie and Billy Bathgate offer prominent company but neither is likely to contest the lead aggressively over this extended 1m4½f trip on Standard to Slow ground. With Romantic Spirit able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front, the race is set up for a steady-tempo affair where the leader can conserve energy before kicking turning in — conditions that typically punish true hold-up horses who need a genuinely fast pace to make their ground. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Big Win, Free World, It's Only Fun, Cavalry Call, Elemental Eye and Character Testing are all natural closers who will find themselves compressed into midfield positions, unable to race from their ideal spot, which dilutes the threat of the hold-up brigade as a collective. This race shape strongly favours horses who can track Romantic Spirit close to the pace — prominent and second-wave stalkers who get a soft lead to chase rather than a true stomp to pounce on.

watchPoints.text: Romantic Spirit's sectional control is the axis of the entire race — if he builds even a two-length lead by the halfway point unchallenged, the hold-up horses compressed into midfield will find it extremely difficult to close the gap on Standard to Slow ground.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Big Win, It's Only Fun, Cavalry Call, Elemental Eye, Character Testing) all wanting to race from the rear will cause significant traffic congestion in midfield from the first furlong — watch for jockeys being forced wider than ideal or getting boxed in on the rail turning for home.

Jujubella ran just two days ago — monitor early in the race for any sign of fatigue or lack of enthusiasm; a horse returning this quickly in a 14-strong handicap can become an obstacle for those immediately behind her if she fades rapidly.

Billy Bathgate's going statistics (15 from 15 on Standard) are exceptional for a 14-runner field where several rivals have little or no form on this surface — in a scenario where the pace becomes truly honest, his staying power could prove underrated at a big price.

Free World and Natzor both carry fade warnings — if either is placed prominently by their jockeys against their natural style in an attempt to overcome the redistribution problem, they could stop sharply in the final furlong and cause interference for runners finishing behind them.
